verifyFiles.footnote: Checks that every stored piece of every file is still on its platform.

storagePool.title: Storage pool
storagePool.description: Repositories zcrypt manages: auto-created and rotated as they fill up.

tokenScope.shareTitle: Share this account with every user?
tokenScope.unshareTitle: Stop sharing this account with other users?
tokenScope.shareReach: Every user on this instance will upload to and download from this account. Its holder can never see what they store (it is encrypted with keys they do not have) but is the account holder of record for it.
tokenScope.shareQuota: Its quota, rate limits, and any enforcement the platform applies are shared with all of them. One user's abuse can get the whole account restricted.
tokenScope.shareDependence: Files stored through it keep depending on it. Making it local again later cuts those users off from their own files.
tokenScope.unshareAccess: Other users lose access through this account immediately. Their uploads to it stop.
tokenScope.unshareFiles: Any of their files whose chunks live in repositories under this account can no longer be downloaded until it is shared again or the files are re-uploaded elsewhere.
tokenScope.unshareOwner: The owner's own files are not affected.

accountData.label: Your data
accountData.footnote: File contents never pass through zcrypt unencrypted, so they are not in this export: they stay in your storage, readable only with your vault passphrase.

accountData.warnExport: Download your account data first if you want a record of it.

appUpdates.label: App updates
appUpdates.nativePackage: This build doesn't check for updates automatically. It was installed as a native Linux package, which manages updates through your system's package manager instead. Get new releases from <link>{url}/download</link>.
appUpdates.fromAppStore: Updates come from the App Store
appUpdates.footnoteAndroid: Android updates download as a signed APK. Open it to install over this copy; your vault stays in the cloud.
appUpdates.footnote: Updates are signed with zcrypt's release key and verified before install. Only builds signed with that key are ever accepted.
appUpdates.reinstallNote: Installed before v0.1.7? Older copies were signed with a different key, so Android will refuse the update with "App not installed". Let pending uploads finish, uninstall zcrypt once, then install the download and sign back in. Every update after that installs in place.

steps.s2: Add innocent-looking fake files to the decoy vault.

steps.s4: The attacker sees the fake files; your real vault stays hidden.
steps.s5: There is no way for an attacker to tell the difference.
